correctness.rationale: For each potential directed r-cycle, conditioning fixes exactly one outgoing and one incoming edge at its r vertices; all other incident edges remain fair. This gives the exact binomial score difference, all n,r,k. Algebra proves the sign and square-zero classification. A deterministic transitive-triple count makes the centered triangle count a score-histogram linear statistic, and the cycle/score covariance ratios give its exact L2 projection. Independent exhaustive enumeration for n=3,4,5,6 plus arithmetic tests through n=120 passed 41341 assertions; finite tests are not used as an infinite proof.

evidence: Gao–McKay–Wang (2000) gives asymptotic conditional counts for prescribed score sequences and digraphs, per the publisher abstract; no exact finite joint formula is established by that abstract.
Janson (1995) states a normal limit for Hamilton-cycle counts; full text was not available, so broad projection overlap remains unverified.
Full text of Kolesnik–Sanchez, arXiv:2009.09322v1, sections 1–3, proves score-sequence realizability using zonotopes, not score-class/cycle covariance.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A general projection or conditioned-digraph enumeration theorem could potentially subsume the statement; the inspected accessible full texts do not. Asymptotic conditional-count results cannot alone imply an exact finite-size square-boundary formula. The restricted historical full-text access is explicitly retained as a risk.

originality.rationale: Actual published-finding corpus and prior research records comparisons and inspected primary literature did not establish the explicit all-length score-class covariance or its square-root/perfect-square sign phases. The earlier cycle–triangle Walsh decomposition, combined with a star-support lemma, can imply the residual orthogonality to the score histogram; that projection interpretation is not asserted to be independently new. The new exact covariance and arithmetic classification go beyond the older scalar covariance. Historical priority remains qualified for inaccessible historical full texts.

Gao–McKay–Wang 2000 full text inaccessible; broader conditional subgraph enumeration could give a nontrivial reduction.
General random-tournament pattern-overlap formulas may imply finite moments without matching titles, even though no exact dominating statement was identified.
Pairwise linear orthogonality does not extend to arbitrary measurable score-histogram functions.
